subject: Two geometric invariants over every fixture example: a child's extent lies inside its parent's, and no two siblings claim the same byte.
purpose: Thirty-one rows, three causes, and the sibling half is what earns this oracle. WAS FORTY-FIVE, and 58 before 0a.13: Step 10 cleared FOURTEEN by making the inline phase read requirement 10's content-to-source map, so a continuation line's inline children stop being measured from the block's first-line column and stop reaching outside their own parent. 0a.13 cleared the fourteen that were the emphasis defect, which is the cause the sibling half was written for. Containment alone cannot see the emphasis defect: ***a** gives a Text spanning columns 1..3 and a Strong starting at column 1, and both sit inside their paragraph, so the only statement that catches it is that two nodes claim one byte. That is exactly what it caught, and what 0a.13 then cleared: reverting the emphasis fix makes fourteen rows reappear here, and reverting only the ONE-LINE form of it that the plan originally named leaves SEVEN of the fourteen standing. Measured both ways. This cannot be an upstream comparison either - cmark-gfm re-parents emphasis the same way and takes a link's start from the closing bracket the same way, so it would return agreement on exactly the rows that are wrong. Nodes with no position are skipped, not judged; the 0:0..0:0 sentinel and line zero are scripts/audit-scope-sanity.mjs's subject, and two ratchets that claim the same row can each be satisfied by it moving to the other - which is why the run now reports ZERO skipped child relations where it used to skip the split-off table lead's. Every row's closedBy names the step that is expected to clear it; the three H14 rows name no step because none exists yet, and that is the honest state rather than a guess. EIGHTEEN of the thirty-one are one thing - an autocompleted table cell, which has no source bytes at all - and Step 10 measured both coordinate spellings for it before carrying it rather than taking one: see the recovered-table-cell family in specs/positions/places.json, and Q44.
